title: Making Marie Antoinette: Community Screening (Doc Stories 2026)
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Roman Coppola, first assistant director and producer on Marie Antoinette, and Davia Nelson, creative consultant for Making Marie Antoinette, are expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.In this illuminating behind-the-scenes look at Sofia Coppola’s groundbreaking 2006 period film, Eleanor Coppola reflects, “I love seeing where the illusion of the set meets reality.” That distinction is but one of the fascinating elements of this documentary where actors young and old (Kirsten Dunst, Jason Schwartzman, Asia Argento, and Marianne Faithfull, to name a few) reflect on the experience while still clad in the elaborate costumes and wigs that populate the film (Milena Canonerodeservedly won the Oscar for Best Costume Design). Particularly trenchant is when Coppola catches moments where different crew members —usually men— express how they think things should be done to the nascent young filmmaker. Most touching of all in this posthumous film are Coppola’s reflections from her journal, read by Diane Lane, as she muses about having waited so long to begin her own creative life. —Rod ArmstrongThursday, November 5

title: 14th: Opening Night
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories We are pleased to welcome Director Ava DuVernay for an on stage conversation and Q&A. DuVernay will also be in attendance at the 9:30pm showing for an extended intro.A decade after 13th (Doc Stories, 2016), Ava DuVernay returns to documentary filmmaking with a powerful companion piece examining the 14th Amendment and its enduring influence on American life. While 13th traced the legacy of abolishing slavery and how that amendment intersects with the American carceral system, 14th turns its attention to the sweeping protections enshrined in this vital addition to the US Constitution, including birthright citizenship, equal protection, due process, and limits on the power wielded by heads of state. Timely indeed! DuVernay brings together an extraordinary range of voices to participate in this towering feat of documentation, including Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Stacey Abrams, former Senator Jeff Flake, and historian Eric Foner. Their perspectives illuminate the enduring tensions surrounding a constitutional promise forged during Reconstruction and its continuing significance today. Expansive in scope and deeply engaged with the complexities of American democracy, 14th is a compelling examination of the rights and protections that define American citizenship. —Jessie FairbanksThursday, November 5

title: Shorts Block: New York Times Op Docs
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Directors and film teams from La Retaguardia, The Revolution Against Death, The Tuners, and A Wolf in the Suburbs are expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.Continuing our beloved tradition of a dedicated shorts block featuring new and upcoming films from The New York Times’ Op-Docs desk, this year’s selection offers five singular stories that find humor, humanity, and unexpected drama in the lives of their subjects. A former Olympian wages an unconventional battle to preserve his unruly lawn, while musicians pursue the elusive perfection of pitch at a prestigious piano competition. Amid a national migration crisis, four young Cuban artists make the radical choice to stay. An aging community embarks on an eccentric quest for immortality, while in Sweden, a mother follows a trail of graffiti in hopes of finding her long-lost son. Together, these films celebrate idiosyncratic characters, unexpected passions, and the deeply human impulse to pursue what matters, no matter how improbable the journey. —Jessie FairbanksFilms are in alphabetical order rather than order of play. Total runtime 86 minLa RetaguardiaOlivier Côté, Jean-François Bouchard (Canada, Cuba 2026, 22 min)Amid a national migration crisis, four young Cuban artists go against the tide and choose to stay.The Revolution Against DeathJoshua Oppenheimer (Denmark, Sweden 2026, 23 min)Joshua Oppenheimer gazes into the world of an aging community and their eccentric efforts to achieve immortality.SonLeona Cauklija (Sweden 2026, 13 min)A Swedish mother’s love knows no bounds, using graffiti to track down her long lost son.The TunersPaweł Chorzępa (Poland 2026, 23 min)Distinguished tuners work tirelessly to achieve perfect pitch for their instruments at a renowned piano competition.A Wolf in the SuburbsAmélie Hardy (Canada 2026, 18 min)A Mississaugan man revives his former Olympian mindset in a fight to preserve his lawn’s overgrowth.Friday, November 6

title: Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Everyone quoted in this vastly entertaining film, from Bruce Springsteen to Bette Midler, agrees that Darlene Love has the best voice in music. Born in 1941, Love has lived a big life with its concomitant ups and downs. From a dreadful contract with Phil Spector where she rarely got credit for songs she sang lead vocals on to a period cleaning houses in Beverly Hills to her rediscovery and eventual admittance to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the movie wisely lets Love herself chart her career, leading with joy and humor rather than anger and bitterness. In addition to wonderful archival material and Love’s poignant reminiscences, I Know Where I’ve Been incorporates present-day studio performances by the 85-year-old powerhouse singing many of her classic tracks. A toe-tapping tribute to one of the unsung singers of our time, this documentary serves as evidence that, though it might take a while, sometimes dreams do come true. This star-studded portrait features contemporary interviews with Cher, Paul Shaffer, Dionne Warwick, and David Letterman, and is produced by Taraji P, Henson and Jeffrey Latimer.—Rod ArmstrongFriday, November 6

title: Shorts Block: Sensory Experience
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Directors and film teams from Chuuraa, Listen, Pelo Lindo, Still Standing, They're Here, and You Do Not Exist are expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.This cinematic collection of six films explores the act of sensing as a way of connecting with the world around us. Through immersive soundscapes, close observation, and distinct points of view, these filmmakers turn attention into revelation, drawing us closer to what might otherwise remain unseen, unheard, or forgotten. Moving between intimate memory and collective experience, they listen closely to the vanishing sounds of nature, look beneath what appears intact, uncover what has been buried by time, and bear witness to what can be taken or erased. As the world keeps moving, these films reveal what persists and how holding onto what remains can become an act of resistance. —Mariana FinelliFilms are in alphabetical order rather than order of play. Total runtime 100 minChuuraaEvgenia Arbugaeva (UK 2026, 18 min)A Sakha scientist journeys into Siberia’s melting permafrost, where the past emerges alongside ancestral beliefs.ListenTaliesin Black-Brown (USA 2026, 15 min)As memory fades and nature changes, an Alaskan sound recordist listens closely to what remains.Pelo LindoJosue Garcia Prado (Guatemala 2026, 24 min)Decades after her son’s forced disappearance, a Guatemalan mother’s enduring faith keeps his memory alive.Still StandingVictor Tadashi Suárez, Livia Albeck-Ripka (USA 2026, 10 min)After the Eaton Fire, Altadena residents confront toxic contamination in homes insurers insist are safe to inhabit.They’re HereLaura Poitras, Rachel Lauren Mueller USA 2026, 25 min)When masked ICE agents descend on Minneapolis, neighbors mobilize, tracking the movements of officers to protect one another.You Do Not ExistDwayne LeBlanc (USA 2026, 8 min)Beneath passing planes, a man reflects on memory, belonging, and the paths not taken.Saturday, November 7

title: Soul Patrol
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Director J.M. Harper and Producer Sam Bisbee are expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.It starts in Vietnam in 1968 with an all-Black six-man patrol team – the first of its kind for this particular war. One of the members, Ed Emmanuel, writes a memoir about the men in 2003, and this moving, creative, and vital documentary depicts their final reunion in 2024. In addition to the veterans’ reminiscences and deep camaraderie, the film incorporates Super 8 footage shot by vets and dramatic reenactments to paint a full picture of these men’s experiences, their lingering traumas, and their continuing friendship. There is darkness, of course – as one of the members reflects, “We survived the war, but there was no peace” – and Soul Patrol doesn’t shy away from the irony of fighting for a country that doesn’t treat Black men well. But the key factor here is recognition – the story of these men and their heroic efforts might have been lost forever without Emmanuel’s book and this seminal film. —Rod ArmstrongSaturday, November 7

title: All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Director Jeanie Finlay is expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.For over 50 years, fisherman Stan Rennie has made his living from Teesside’s waters in North East England. When a mysterious tide of dead sea life washes ashore one night, Stan’s life takes an unexpected turn. As livelihoods begin to disappear and new industrial development emerges along a coastline already scarred by its industrial past, Stan becomes the unlikeliest and most endearing of activists, bringing his community together to uncover what caused the devastating die-offs. Intimate and deeply empathetic, Jeanie Finlay’s documentary captures the community’s grief and collective determination as they exhaust every avenue for answers from those in power. Their search raises larger questions about accountability and what—and who—we are willing to sacrifice in the pursuit of progress. While the river keeps flowing toward the sea, the lives along this coastline are forced to change course. –Mariana FinelliSaturday, November 7

title: Black Sunflowers
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Executive producer Sean Penn joins us in person to introduce the film, followed by a post-screening Q&A with executive producer Dianna Agron, director James Marcus Haney, and documentary participant Anya Diianchuk.In Black Sunflowers, James Marcus Haney drops us into the underground culture of a generation living through wartime Ukraine. Over four years, he follows artists, drifters, soldiers, and friends as they gather in warehouses, fall in love, debate their futures, and find pockets of freedom amid mounting uncertainty. Working with a crew of Ukrainian producers, Haney crafts a kinetic, kaleidoscopic film alive with movement, color, and music. The soundtrack pulses through every frame, turning dance floors into spaces of connection, release, and resistance. Haney’s camera moves with intimacy, capturing the euphoria of collective experience and the violence that threatens to pull these lives apart. The result is an immersive portrait of youth refusing to surrender its vitality, even as the world around them is transformed. Black Sunflowers is a rush of music, movement, and life lived against the clock. —Jessie FairbanksSaturday, November 7

title: Citizen Osama
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Ahmed Hassouna’s striking documentary follows Osama Al-Ashi, a photographer who becomes a war reporter while navigating the first year of his newborn son’s life in northern Gaza. Osama’s work takes him into the devastation surrounding his home, while his responsibilities as a husband and father pull him toward the everyday necessities of keeping his family safe. Hassouna moves fluidly between these two realities, revealing the man behind Osama’s war coverage and the profound personal cost of bearing witness. Selected as Palestine’s official submission to the 2027 Oscars, the filmmaker’s intimate access and restrained approach create an unusually personal portrait of life amid catastrophe, where ordinary acts of care become expressions of perseverance. Citizen Osama is a powerful meditation on the tension between documenting history and maintaining one’s humanity. —Jessie FairbanksSunday, November 8

title: Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Director Erik Shirai is expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.The genesis of sumo was believed to have been a part of a Shinto ritual to appease the gods. Over a century later, it has developed into a beloved sporting tradition with a long lineage of iconic competitors. After reaching a peak in popularity in the 1990s, professional sumo wrestling in the present day faces the crisis of a dwindling talent pool. Through Erik Shirai’s lens, viewers are granted rare access to traditions of the sport originally shrouded in secrecy. Featuring the intimate lives of a group of rikishi (wrestlers) at various stages of their careers, director Shirai paints a comprehensive portrait of the sport’s formidable hierarchy and the fierce training regimen required to ascend to its apex. With sweeping cinematography and moving sound design, Sumo captures the true spirit of its glorious athletes and the art of combat in all its majesty. —Jordan KleinSunday, November 8

title: Boatbuilders
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Director Luke Lorentzen is expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.A visually stunning ode to impeccable craftsmanship and the beauty of Maine, Luke Lorentzen’slatest documentary profiles the workers of Brooklin Boat Yard, a company building custom wooden yachts since 1960. Here, the meticulous employees apply their skills over 16 months to a 56-foot beauty, sawing, sanding, and bending planks to their will. Away from these refined efforts, the men tend to families, gather apples from Maine’s famed orchards, and weather the seasons in a place of remarkable beauty. Lorentzen’s attentive camera also captures workplace potlucks, business meetings, and pep talks from Human Resources, because simmering below the work and the pride they all take in it are the economic challenges and disparities of the modern world amid a very specialized business. As everyone rushes to meet the deadline for the boat’s owner, Boatbuilders manifests a sense of wonder at these vessels of stupendous beauty. —Rod ArmstrongSunday, November 8

title: Tutu: Closing Night
synopsis: Playing as part of 2026 Doc Stories Director Sam Pollard is expected to attend for a post-screening Q&A.Sam Pollard’s intimate documentary immerses the viewer in to the remarkable life of Desmond Tutu, tracing the journey of a young man who became one of South Africa’s most influential voices for justice and reconciliation. Through archival footage, personal reflections, and the testimony of those who knew him, Pollard reveals a man whose convictions were matched by an irrepressible sense of humor and an extraordinary ability to connect with people. Tutu’s role in South Africa’s struggle against apartheid is central, but the film also looks beyond the public figure to explore his family, faith, friendships, and the private costs of a life lived so visibly. The result is a richly human portrait of a complicated, charismatic man who understood that moral courage could coexist with joy. —Jessie FairbanksSunday, November 8

title: De Gaulle: Part 1 – Resistance
synopsis: Playing as part of Bay Area French Film Festival (Nov. 13 -15, 2026) The first chapter of Antonin Baudry’s ambitious two-part historical drama follows Charles de Gaulle in the early years of World War II, as France faces collapse and occupation. Set against the turmoil of war, De Gaulle: Part 1 – Resistanceexplores the making of a leader, the birth of a political vision, and the fight to keep hope alive in one of France’s darkest moments. Both intimate and epic in scope, the film brings a pivotal moment of French history to the screen with intensity and scale.Friday, November 13

title: De la Comédie Française
synopsis: Playing as part of Bay Area French Film Festival (Nov. 13 -15, 2026)At the Comédie-Française, there is one golden rule: the play is never canceled. Unfortunately for Nina, everything else is—just three hours before the premiere of her first staging. An actor is stuck on a train, tensions explode, equipment breaks down, egos clash, and panic sets in. With no way out and time slipping away, Nina must hold the show together at all costs. Will she make it until the curtain rises?Saturday, November 14

title: Women on Trial
synopsis: Playing as part of Bay Area French Film Festival (Nov. 13 -15, 2026)A landmark trial shakes France when young Marie-Claire is prosecuted for having an illegal abortion. Defended by Gisèle Halimi, a fearless French-Tunisian lawyer portrayed by Charlotte Gainsbourg, the women challenge a male-dominated justice system and fight for reproductive rights. Their groundbreaking case helps pave the way for the 1975 Veil Act, which legalizes abortion in France.Saturday, November 14

title: Another Day
synopsis: Playing as part of Bay Area French Film Festival (Nov. 13 -15, 2026)Selected for the 2026 Cannes Film Festival competition, Jeanne Herry’s Garance (Another Day) follows a young actress, played by Adèle Exarchopoulos, struggling to navigate life, love, and addiction. Spanning eight turbulent years of relationships, friendships, parties, and personal upheavals, the film explores a woman’s search for freedom and identity as alcohol increasingly takes control of her life. Raw, vibrant, and deeply human, this intimate drama captures the exhilarating and destructive sides.Sunday, November 15

title: Family Quiz
synopsis: Playing as part of Bay Area French Film Festival (Nov. 13 -15, 2026)Stan, a working-class outsider, meets his girlfriend’s cultured and intimidating family for the first time.
